what_its_for: Aliskiren is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by blocking a substance in your body called renin, which helps relax and widen your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take aliskiren by mouth once a day, with or without food. However, try to take it the same way each time — either always with food or always without food, because food can affect how well the medicine works. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 150 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 300 mg once daily if your blood pressure is not controlled well enough. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store aliskiren at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-fat meals right before or with your dose, as fatty foods can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed. Do not drink grapefruit juice or eat large amounts of grapefruit while taking this medicine, as it may affect how the drug works. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor approves, as they can raise potassium levels to a dangerous point. Do not use other blood pressure medicines that block the renin-angiotensin system — such as ACE inhibitors (like lisinopril) or ARBs (like losartan) — at the same time, especially if you have diabetes or kidney disease. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause dizziness. Do not use NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without asking your doctor first, as they can reduce the effectiveness of this medicine and harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (which could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness or tingling; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; severe diarrhea or vomiting leading to dehydration; or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Also contact your doctor if your blood pressure readings remain high or if you have any new or bothersome symptoms.
when_it_works: Aliskiren starts working to lower your blood pressure within a few hours of taking your first dose, but it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit. Even if you feel well and do not notice symptoms, it is very important to keep taking this medicine every day as directed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking aliskiren without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take aliskiren if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. If you become pregnant, stop taking it immediately and contact your doctor right away. Breastfeeding: It is not known if aliskiren passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: Aliskiren is not recommended for children under 18 years of age. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and dizziness. Use with caution and follow your doctor's guidance. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Diabetes: Patients with diabetes should NOT use aliskiren together with ACE inhibitors or ARBs due to a higher risk of kidney failure, low blood pressure, and dangerous increases in potassium levels.
